candidates.label: xyB (B only, location-based second b/d capture)
candidates.change: rev0 B zombie_entry rewritten. Captured zom20b/d (CX=0; BX = its load address+3, preserved by its stosw loop) publishes (BX+0FDh) XOR 0CCCCh to arena cell [4A19h] at its 4th instruction and searches EB F9 CC CC backward from its own base+100h (below its own four tails), replacement jmp [4A17h], bp 3400h (the 0E070E17 counter-bomb is dropped). Captured zom20a (CX!=0) reads [4A19h] XOR 0CCCCh as DI at its 10th instruction (unset cell = CC fill -> DI=0 = rev0 top-down search), INT87 at its 12th (rev0 13th), bp 2000h. Intent: when one tail consumer (MOV_AX_WIN, LowKey, TOM_anonymous, a V6 B) took the top dead tail before our B startup search, B captures the upper zombie X directly and X + zom20a then do the two-step on the lower zombie Y (dead Y+165h, live Y+14Ch).

candidates.label: ctlB (layout control, measurement only)
candidates.change: xyB with the location feature disabled at identical size and instruction counts: b/d path writes the unread cell [4A1Bh] and uses lea di,[0000h] (top-down search like rev0); zom20a reads the never-written [4A19h] -> DI=0.
candidates.groupNotes: threat ity8i (same cohorts as evtia): ALL -0.0035 [-0.0189,+0.0120] W/L 4/5; MOV_AX_WIN +0.004, LowKey -0.017, TOM_anonymous +0.008, lead_V6 -0.010. Layout change and dropping the 0E070E17 counter-bomb are neutral here; xyB minus ctl = -0.062 on the same cohorts.

candidates.label: xyK (diagnostic: kill Y instead of capturing it)
candidates.change: xyB, but when the cell is set the zom20a search uses BX:CX=0 (kills Y's live tail) instead of jmp [4A17h]; unset cell still captures as rev0.
candidates.groupNotes: threat r7ssq (same cohorts): ALL -0.0198 [-0.0418,+0.0022] W/L 2/11; MOV_AX_WIN -0.0125, LowKey -0.056, TOM_anonymous -0.011, lead_V6 0. Ordering ctl (-0.003) > xyK (-0.020) > xyB (-0.066): capturing a second b/d zombie costs ~0.046 more than killing it, and removing Y as a wild zombie costs ~0.017 (n.s.).

threatFindings.threat: The card's zrl03-style two-step (first search kills the top dead tail, second captures the live tail) is missing in rev0.
threatFindings.evidence: Static: rev0 already does it. B's startup INT87 (12th instr, from DI=0 backward) patches the topmost tail, which with no earlier consumer is the dead +165h of the upper zombie X (zom20b/d tails +11Ah/+133h/+14Ch/+165h are byte-identical in a +-6 byte window and the top 4-byte context is identical too, so no single 4-byte pattern can pick the live +14Ch); the captured zom20a's search then takes X+14Ch. With exactly one earlier consumer (HRZ_MOV_AX_WIN instr 6 BX:CX=0, HRZ_LowKey_WBB1 instr 9 BX:CX=0, TOM_anonymous2 ~instr 10 FF 26 patch, a V6-family B in the same round) B's own search takes X+14Ch directly. INT 87h does not report the match address (Cpu.java int87), so the kill cannot be turned into a direct write.
threatFindings.impact: none; no new defense needed for the k=0/k=1 cases

threatFindings.threat: Lower b/d zombie Y is never captured; capturing it via the captured zombie's own location (BX = load address+3) would add value.
threatFindings.evidence: xyB implements it and loses: screen 20261004002159767-A027-screen-6o11d ALL -0.0226 [-0.0397,-0.0055]; threat 20261004002159907-A027-threat-evtia ALL -0.066 [-0.105,-0.027] (LowKey -0.138, TOM_anonymous -0.100) vs layout control ity8i -0.003.
threatFindings.impact: harmful: about -0.06 in cohorts with one early tail consumer, -0.02 on field S

threatFindings.threat: A second captured b/d zombie harms our team (both captured b/d run zombie phoenix with bp 3400h from the same get_ip base, so X and Y target the same anchor and collide, or their streams kill B).
threatFindings.evidence: Indirect only: on identical cohorts xyB (capture Y) -0.066, xyK (kill Y) -0.020, ctl -0.003 (jobs evtia, r7ssq, ity8i). Not traced.
threatFindings.impact: ~0.046 in early-consumer cohorts; would also apply to any design that captures more than one b/d zombie on the same lattice point

threatFindings.threat: A wild (uncaptured) zom20b/d helps us by killing opponents with its 16 fixed word writes; removing it costs.
threatFindings.evidence: xyK minus ctl = -0.017 [n.s.] on the same 24 cohorts (r7ssq vs ity8i).

threatFindings.threat: 2025 b/d tail competitors: MOV_AX_WIN (instr 6, kill), LowKey_WBB1 (instr 9, kill), TOM_anonymous2 (~instr 10, FF 26 patch) all consume the top tail before our B startup search (instr 12).
threatFindings.evidence: Static disassembly (dis86) of official-2025/survivors-online binaries; rev0 is unaffected by them in practice: ctl and base equal within noise on their cohorts (ity8i).
threatFindings.impact: parity shift only; rev0 still captures X in these battles

recommendation: do not promote. xyB is clearly negative (screen ALL -0.023, lo < 0; threat -0.066). rev0 already implements the two-step b/d capture the card describes; the only extra target (the lower zombie Y) is not worth capturing with the current zombie phoenix. If anyone revisits multi-zombie capture, give each captured b/d its own lattice offset first and trace it. Close the card.
